content:
**DOCTRINE — migration version numbers are content-identifiers, NEVER reused; the gap is honest record; retire-by-deletion includes the version slot (monotonic-forever)**

What: Human ruling at A2 (#231). A migration version number is a CONTENT-IDENTIFIER and is NEVER reused. Pinned when deciding the version for the new governance.approvedLabel config entry after C4 removed the never-shipped 0.6.0 (memory.dualWrite) entry.

RULING: governance.approvedLabel takes 0.7.0, NOT the freed 0.6.0 slot.

WHY: a reused 0.6.0 would name two indistinguishable states depending on WHEN it was applied — the exact ambiguity content-hashing exists to prevent. Critically, THIS repo ran under 0.6.0-dualWrite during the cutover window; that window's archaeology needs 0.6.0 to mean ONE thing. The gap at 0.6 is NOT a tolerable cost to avoid — it IS honest record: a hole in the migration sequence is the visible, log-readable mark of a retirement.

DOCTRINE (fixed for all future retirements): retire-by-deletion includes the version slot; the migration sequence is MONOTONIC-FOREVER (numbers only ever go up, gaps are permanent and meaningful). Extends [[architecture/config-key-retirement-doctrine]] (never-shipped keys retire by deletion) — now: their version number retires with them.

Where: brain/core/config-migrations.mjs (chain currently 0.1.0→0.5.0 after C4's 0.6.0 removal; A2 appends 0.7.0). Related: [[sdd/issue-229-c4/done]], [[sdd/issue-231-a2/kickoff]].
